title: When Safety Speaks a Language: A Mechanistic Analysis of Safety-Language Identity Entanglement in LLMs
abstract: arXiv:2608.29936v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Safety alignment of large language models (LLMs) degrades across languages, yet the internal mechanism driving this asymmetry remains poorly understood. Our work, therefore, presents a systematic mechanistic analysis of multilingual safety using sparse autoencoder (SAE) features, sparse interpretable directions in the residual stream associated with harmful and harmless model behavior across three instruction-tuned LLMs, eight languages, and all model layers. We observe that safety-relevant features are architecture-dependent in terms of where they are located and how they are distributed across layers. Additionally, they are geometrically entangled with language identity and exhibit cross-lingual sharing patterns, i.e., languages share safety features to varying degrees across model depths and architectures. This safety-language entanglement has direct consequences such that ablating safety features impacts not only harmful response rat

translated_title: 当安全说一种语言时：大语言模型中安全与语言身份纠缠的机制分析
translated_abstract: 大语言模型（LLM）的安全对齐在不同语言间会出现退化，然而驱动这种不对称性的内部机制仍然知之甚少。因此，我们的工作利用稀疏自编码器（SAE）特征对多语言安全进行了系统的机制分析，这些特征是残差流中与模型有害及无害行为相关的稀疏可解释方向，研究覆盖三个指令微调的LLM、八种语言以及所有模型层。我们观察到，安全相关特征在其所在位置和跨层分布方面依赖于模型架构。此外，这些特征与语言身份在几何上相互纠缠，并表现出跨语言共享模式，即不同语言在模型的不同深度和不同架构上以不同程度共享安全特征。这种安全-语言纠缠具有直接的后果，例如消融安全特征不仅会影响有害响应率……
tldr: 本文通过稀疏自编码器特征的机制分析发现，LLM中的安全特征与语言身份在几何上纠缠并以依赖架构的方式跨语言共享，从而揭示了安全对齐跨语言退化背后的内部机制。
en_tdlr: This mechanistic analysis using sparse autoencoder features reveals that safety features in LLMs are geometrically entangled with language identity and shared across languages in an architecture-dependent manner, explaining why safety alignment degrades across languages.
